steps.title: In the ground
steps.text: Cadmium has no mines of its own. It replaces a little of the zinc in sphalerite, the main zinc ore: a few kilograms in every tonne of zinc concentrate.

steps.title: Ride with zinc
steps.text: Zinc ore is mined, floated and sent to a smelter, where the concentrate is roasted and dissolved in sulphuric acid. Cadmium dissolves along with the zinc.
steps.india: Hindustan Zinc's smelting carries cadmium, but the Indian Bureau of Mines recorded no domestic production in 2020-21 or 2021-22.

steps.title: Extract
steps.text: Before zinc can be plated out, the solution must be cleaned. Zinc dust is stirred in, and cadmium, being the less reactive metal, drops out as a sponge. Smelters must remove it either way: cadmium is toxic and would spoil the zinc.

steps.title: Refine
steps.text: The sponge is dissolved again and plated by electrolysis, or distilled, since cadmium boils at only 767°C. It is cast into sticks and balls.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Nickel-cadmium batteries take the most: rugged cells for aircraft, railways and backup power. Cadmium telluride is the absorber in thin-film solar panels. Pigments, coatings and alloys take the rest, though many of these uses are restricted because cadmium is toxic.
steps.india: Imported 6,374 tonnes in 2021-22, mainly from South Korea, Japan and Russia.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Nickel-cadmium batteries are collected and the cadmium distilled out for reuse; rules in many countries require it. Old cadmium telluride panels are taken back by their makers.
